+# xfo-miner v1.0.4
+
+This release focuses on OTA delivery reliability and release artifact consistency across Linux, Windows, and manual operator installs.
+
+## Highlights
+
+- Fixed Linux OTA extraction handoff where the updater could download and unpack the archive successfully but still fail with:
+  - `main binary not found in extracted archive`
+- OTA now correctly handles release archives whose extracted binary uses a platform-specific filename such as:
+  - `xfo-miner-linux-amd64`
+  - `xfo-miner-windows-amd64.exe`
+- Release packages now include `config.example.json` at the archive root for all supported platforms.
+
+## OTA Reliability Improvements
+
+- The updater now recognizes both:
+  - the currently running executable basename
+  - the standard packaged platform binary name for the current OS/arch
+- This closes the mismatch between release artifact structure and OTA binary lookup logic.
+- Added regression coverage to ensure OTA updates continue to work even when the downloaded archive contains the standard packaged binary name instead of a bare `xfo-miner` filename.
+
+## Custom Executable Name Safety
+
+- Confirmed and locked in the OTA contract that updates always replace and restart using the currently running executable path.
+- This means operators who rename the miner binary to a custom filename keep that custom path across OTA replacement, as long as the archive contains a valid main miner binary.
+- Added regression coverage for custom executable path preservation during archive-based OTA updates.
+
+## Release Package Improvements
+
+- All generated `.tar.gz` and `.zip` release artifacts now ship with:
+  - the platform binary
+  - `config.example.json`
+- This improves first-run operator experience for manual downloads and unpacked installations.
+
+## Validation and Test Coverage
+
+- Added updater regression coverage for:
+  - platform-packaged archive binary discovery
+  - custom executable path preservation during OTA swap
+- Verified with:
+  - `go test ./...`
+
+## Operator Notes
+
+- This release is intended to become the new OTA baseline for Linux miners that previously failed after archive extraction.
+- `config.example.json` is now bundled in release artifacts for manual installation convenience, but OTA still only replaces the main miner binary at runtime.
